\section{Reversible chains and Dirichlet forms}
\label{sec:markov-intro}

\begin{definition}
\label{def:dirichlet}
Let $P$ be an irreducible transition matrix on a finite state space $\Omega$
that is reversible with respect to its stationary distribution $\pi$. For any
function $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, the \emph{Dirichlet form} is
\[
\mathcal{E}_P(f,f) = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{x,y \in \Omega} \pi(x) P(x,y) \bigl(f(x) - f(y)\bigr)^2,
\]
and the \emph{spectral gap} is
$\gamma(P) = \inf \{ \mathcal{E}_P(f,f) / \operatorname{Var}_\pi(f) : \operatorname{Var}_\pi(f) > 0 \}$.
\end{definition}

\section{Spectral gap comparison}
\label{sec:gap-results}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:spectral-gap}
Let $P$ and $\widetilde{P}$ be irreducible reversible Markov chains on
$\Omega$ with stationary distributions $\pi$ and $\widetilde{\pi}$, and let
$\mathcal{E}_P, \mathcal{E}_{\widetilde{P}}, \gamma(P), \gamma(\widetilde{P})$
be given by Definition~\ref{def:dirichlet}. Suppose there exist constants
$c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that $\mathcal{E}_{\widetilde{P}}(f,f) \le c_1 \mathcal{E}_P(f,f)$
for all $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\widetilde{\pi}(x) \ge c_2 \pi(x)$
for all $x \in \Omega$. Then
\[
\gamma(\widetilde{P}) \le \frac{c_1}{c_2} \gamma(P).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For any nonconstant $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, the variational formula for
variance gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\widetilde{\pi}}(f)
= \min_{a \in \mathbb{R}} \sum_{x \in \Omega} \widetilde{\pi}(x)(f(x) - a)^2
\ge c_2 \min_{a \in \mathbb{R}} \sum_{x \in \Omega} \pi(x)(f(x) - a)^2
= c_2 \operatorname{Var}_\pi(f).
\]
Dividing $\mathcal{E}_{\widetilde{P}}(f,f) \le c_1 \mathcal{E}_P(f,f)$ by
$\operatorname{Var}_{\widetilde{\pi}}(f) \ge c_2 \operatorname{Var}_\pi(f)$ and
taking the infimum over nonconstant $f$ gives $\gamma(\widetilde{P}) \le (c_1/c_2)\gamma(P)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[{\cite[Theorem~2.1]{nord2024operator}}]
\label{prop:comparison}
Let $P$ and $\widetilde{P}$ share the stationary distribution $\pi$. If each
transition of $\widetilde{P}$ is routed along a canonical path of transitions
of $P$ with congestion constant $A > 0$, then
$\mathcal{E}_{\widetilde{P}}(f,f) \le A \mathcal{E}_P(f,f)$ for all
$f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\gamma(\widetilde{P}) \le A \gamma(P)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Expanding $f(x) - f(y)$ telescopically along each canonical path and applying
the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality yields
$\mathcal{E}_{\widetilde{P}}(f,f) \le A \mathcal{E}_P(f,f)$. Since
$\widetilde{\pi} = \pi$, applying Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral-gap} with
$c_1 = A$ and $c_2 = 1$ gives $\gamma(\widetilde{P}) \le A \gamma(P)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:mixing}
Under the path-congestion hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:comparison}, if
$\gamma(\widetilde{P}) > 0$ then the relaxation time of $P$ satisfies
$\gamma(P)^{-1} \le A \gamma(\widetilde{P})^{-1}$, and its $L^2$-mixing time
at threshold $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ obeys
\[
t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(2)}(P, \varepsilon)
\le \frac{A}{\gamma(\widetilde{P})} \log\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon \pi_{\min}}\right),
\]
where $\pi_{\min} = \min_{x \in \Omega} \pi(x)$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Rearranging $\gamma(\widetilde{P}) \le A \gamma(P)$ yields
$\gamma(P)^{-1} \le A \gamma(\widetilde{P})^{-1}$. Combining this bound with
the standard spectral-gap $L^2$-mixing estimate in
\cite[Proposition~4.3]{hale2023bounds} gives the stated inequality.
\end{proof}
